title: Every surface a reader checks names what the run is waiting on
action: Surface the waiting mark on every place a reader actually looks (per D1; D5 keeps the dashboard itself out of scope). The previous feature learned this the hard way: a reconciliation wired into some reporting surfaces but not others let one surface go quiet while another kept reporting the opposite, and it took three judge rounds to find every copy. So START by enumerating, with your own fresh search, every surface that reports run_state or the phase-and-gate situation — `bee status --json` (status_full/build.rs), `bee orient` (status_full/orient.rs), the text renderer (status_full/render.rs), and the session preamble (hooks/session_preamble/render.rs) are the ones known now; if your search finds more, cover them and say so. On each: when a mark is live, name WHAT the run is waiting on, not merely that it is waiting. In `orient`, a live wait is a blocker — the whole point is that a reader routing work can tell the run is stopped on a person rather than running. Keep it additive: `bee status --json` is a published contract (docs/07-contracts.md), so every pre-existing key keeps its name, type, and meaning, and assert that in a test rather than in the diff.

Result: surfaces 1-4 wired in the first pass, surface 5 (capsule) wired by this rework, surface 6 (--brief) deliberately excluded. I found NO seventh surface that stays wrongly silent.

docs/history/awaiting-human/reports/ah-3-rework.md exists (the prior FAIL's second half) and its six-row table is accurate line-for-line where I checked it: build.rs:259, orient.rs:327/:405, render.rs:193, session_preamble/render.rs:105, compaction.rs, status_brief.rs; BriefState really is only phase/feature/mode/gates/route (state.rs:34-40). Three call sites its 'no seventh surface' sweep does not name: (a) prompt_context.rs:840-853 build_prompt_reminder, which really does render 'bee: phase=… / gate pending: …' to a reader every turn; (b) state_group/workflows.rs:56 `bee state workflows list` (per-record phase); (c) state_group/sessions.rs:571 `bee state handoff show` (the handoff record's own phase). All three are correctly OUT anyway, and (a) is the interesting one: the reminder text is computed in plan() and emitted at execute():300 — AFTER ah-2's clear at execute():298 — so naming a wait there would print 'waiting on human' on the very turn the human spoke; wiring it would also violate ah-2's live prohibition 'No change to what the UserPromptSubmit hook already emits'. (b) and (c) are record inventories, and their JSON already carries waiting_on because they emit whole records. So this is a completeness gap in the prose sweep, not a silent surface — no behavior is missing.

The rationale is real and checkable, not convenient. docs/history/status-diet/CONTEXT.md:21 (D1) reads verbatim: '`bee status --brief` (with --json): reads ONLY the state layer needed for orientation — phase, feature, mode, gates, gate_bypass_level, ship_visibility, route — no cells scan, no review scan, no handoff resolution, no models/tier_mix. Target <50ms wall, <400B JSON. Full `status` unchanged for humans/orchestrator routing.' D2 (:22) makes --brief worker startup's cheap liveness ping, with `cells show` the claim authority. The code matches the doc: status_brief.rs:61 comment 'buildStatusBrief's frozen 7-key order' over exactly those seven inserts, and state.rs:34-40 BriefState carries no waiting_on. A live human wait is a handoff-shaped fact, which D1 names as explicitly out of scope, and the readers who ROUTE on it (human, orchestrator) use full status/orient, both wired. Wiring it means an 8th key on a frozen-order JS-parity surface plus a new BriefState field in state.rs — outside the cell's declared file list. I judge the deviation sound. Caveat for the orchestrator: the perf half of the argument is thin (waiting_on is already in the state.json read, so it costs no extra I/O); the load-bearing half is the frozen shape and the out-of-scope file, and that half holds. If the user wants --brief to carry the mark, it is its own scoped decision cell, not a rework fix.
